V</cite> (<cite ref="Tosefta Avodah Zarah 6:6">VI</cite>), 6 <he>בי מוסייאות … שעת הש׳ אע״פ שעבר הש׳ וכ׳</he> altars which gentiles have put up at a time of religious persecution are forbidden (as to the use of the materials) even after the persecution is over; Y. ib. V, 45ᵃ top; Bab.

<cite ref="Tosefta Shabbat 15:17">Tosef. Sabb. XV</cite> (<cite ref="Tosefta Shabbat 16:17">XVI</cite>), 17 <he>במה דברים אמורים שלא בשעת הש׳ אבל בשעת הש׳ וכ׳</he> this (that one may violate religious laws to save his life) is said only when there is no general religious persecution, but during a persecution one must give up his life even for the least essential law; <cite ref="Sanhedrin 74a">Snh. 74ᵃ</cite> Ms. M. (ed. <he>גזירת המלכות</he>).

<cite ref="Shir HaShirim Rabbah 2:5">Cant. R. to II, 5</cite> <he>שלפי הש׳</he>, v. <cite ref="U01372"><he>שֶׁלֶף</he></cite>; <cite ref="Shabbat 60a">Sabb. 60ᵃ</cite> Ms. M. (ed. <he>הגזרה</he>); a. fr.—Pl. <cite ref="U01527"><he>שְׁמָדִים</he></cite>, <cite ref="U01527"><he>שְׁמָדִין</he></cite>.

<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 67:7">Gen. R. s. 67</cite> (ref. to <cite ref="Genesis 27:40">Gen. XXVII, 40</cite>) <he>אם ראית … גזור עליו ש׳ וכ׳</he> when thou (Esau-Rome) seest thy brother (Jacob) cast off the yoke of the Law, decree persecutions over him, and thou shalt have power over him.
<cite ref="Midrash Tehillim 18:9">Midr. Till. to Ps. XVIII, 5</cite> <he>שכמה ש׳ גזרו עלינו בימיה</he> for they decreed many persecutions over us in her (Rome’s) days; a. e.
